n1: The traces consistently identify a white disc in the edited image, but they may be binding to the wrong object: the source shows a small square DVD case near the center and a black animal-like object to its right, while the edit shows two white discs and no clearly corresponding case. The question “What color is the DVD?” does not establish which edited object is the DVD or whether the original DVD itself was recolored; the binding’s “black DVD” premise is also not supported by the source image. Tighten the node’s target binding to the source object using its visible location/appearance and require comparison with that same object in the edit, distinguishing a transformed target from newly appearing or duplicated discs. Preserve the complete/partial/absent/unknown distinctions and assess whether any requested change to the bound target is evidenced; do not infer completion merely from a white disc elsewhere. The repeated high-confidence traces are not independent confirmation of correct identity. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth, so investigate this identity/evidence mismatch rather than forcing “no.” No transport or dependency failures are reported.

The binding is already specific, and the repeated traces consistently report the bound square case is not identifiable in the edit; the white round discs are elsewhere and do not establish progress on the requested DVD. Preserve the identity-and-same-target requirement, but make the node’s outcome criteria explicitly distinguish *unidentifiable target* from *confirmed unchanged target*: use unresolved/unknown when identity or change cannot be established, and absent only when the same DVD is identifiable and remains black/unchanged. This avoids converting missing visual evidence into a negative finding while still treating unrelated discs as no evidence of progress. The traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure; confidence and repeated agreement do not resolve the identity ambiguity.

The node’s target binding is ambiguous and appears inconsistent with the images: the source shows a small square DVD case near the center, while the edited image shows two circular discs, one white near center-left and another white near center-right. The traces repeatedly call the center-right disc the DVD and report complete, but do not establish which edited object corresponds to the source DVD/case; the aggregate “yes” therefore conflicts with the reference “no” without identifying the visual failure. Tighten the binding to the source object using its location/appearance and require comparison with that same object in the edited image, rather than accepting any white disc as the target. Make the criterion explicitly distinguish complete, partial, absent, and unresolved based on visible evidence of the bound object’s color change; if correspondence cannot be established, return unknown rather than infer completion. Investigate the apparent extra disc/object and the source-to-edit correspondence, but do not treat repeated high-confidence traces as proof or force a “no” solely to match the reference. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
